title: Pagoda of Fogong Temple (Yingxian Wooden Pagoda)
summary: The Sakyamuni Pagoda of Fogong Temple in Yingxian county, Shanxi, was built in 1056 under the Liao dynasty. It is a nine-storey wooden pagoda 67.31 m high with a base diameter of 30.27 m, described by China's UNESCO tentative-list entry as the oldest and tallest wooden multi-storey structure in the world.

uncertainty.note: Built 1056 (UNESCO tentative list; China Daily); a renovation completed in 1195 is reported by Chinabound. End is the present.

reviewer_note: Shape tower. Height 67.31 m is in both the UNESCO tentative-list entry and China Daily; Chinabound gives 65.84 m for the same pagoda with the same 30.27 m base diameter, so the height is disputed and the UNESCO figure was used. The 30.27 m base diameter is from China Daily only. The 1195 renovation rests on Chinabound alone. Wooden material rests on China Daily's headline description (wooden pagoda, nailless).
